events.title: Google releases Gemini 3.7 Flash — agentic/coding workhorse tier at 50% intro price
events.summary: Google shipped Gemini 3.7 Flash three weeks after 3.6 Flash, positioned as its most intelligent workhorse model for coding and agents. Day-one GA in Gemini API/AI Studio and same-day availability in GitHub Copilot. Intro pricing $0.75/M input and $3.75/M output through 2026-12-31, then $1.50/$7.50.
events.why_it_matters: Sub-$1/M input for near-frontier agentic scores changes model-selection defaults for high-volume agent loops; the 3-week Flash cadence is itself a competitive-velocity signal.

events.title: DeepSeek V4-Pro GA — native OpenAI Responses API support, agent benchmarks, off-peak pricing
events.summary: DeepSeek moved V4-Pro from preview to GA across app/web/API (deepseek-v4-pro) with native OpenAI Responses API support and a one-click Codex configuration. Thinking-effort levels (low/high/max) added for V4-Pro and V4-Flash. Peak/off-peak pricing takes effect 2026-08-16T16:00Z with off-peak at 50% of peak.
events.why_it_matters: Responses-API compatibility makes DeepSeek a near-drop-in inside OpenAI-native agent stacks. Confirmed peak/off-peak rates (effective 2026-08-16T16:00Z) are a large increase vs current flat rates — V4-Pro output rises from $0.87 to $3.96/Mtok peak / $1.98 off-peak — so budget-sensitive agent workloads now need time-of-day scheduling or re-evaluation.
events.update_2026_08_16: Exact peak/off-peak rates confirmed from official pricing docs during 2026-08-16T00:00Z run. Net effect is a substantial price increase, not a discount: even off-peak V4-Pro output is ~2.3x the current flat rate, and peak is ~4.6x. Peak windows align with China business hours (09:00-12:00 / 14:00-18:00 Beijing). Concurrency limits unchanged: flash 2500, pro 500.

events.title: OpenAI previews Ultrafast mode — GPT-5.6 Sol served on Cerebras at up to 750 tok/s (~14x)
events.published_at_note: Timing discrepancy: TechCrunch article published 2026-08-13T19:22Z; openai.com/index/previewing-ultrafast/ page metadata shows publishedTime 2026-08-11T10:00Z. Staged announcement likely; treated as Aug 11-13 boundary event.
events.summary: OpenAI announced a preview of Ultrafast mode, serving GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 output tokens/sec (~14x standard) with inference powered by Cerebras wafer-scale hardware rather than GPUs. Access limited to a small preview group; pricing undisclosed.
events.why_it_matters: First time OpenAI serves its frontier model on third-party non-GPU inference silicon — validates alternative inference silicon at frontier quality and signals speed-tiered API products as the next competitive axis.

events.title: GitHub Copilot weekly release — Agent Plugins 1.0 GA, Kimi K3 rollout, Ollama BYOK in JetBrains
events.summary: Agent Plugins 1.0 went GA (build once, run across VS Code, Copilot CLI, Copilot SDK, Copilot app). Kimi K3 and MAI-Code-1.1-Flash rolled out across paid plans. Copilot CLI gained /tasks subagent view, --plan + --mode autopilot headless combos, /rewind. JetBrains added cross-session memory and Ollama as BYOK provider.
events.why_it_matters: Portable plugins are Copilot's play for an agent-ecosystem standard competing with MCP; Ollama BYOK in JetBrains signals local-model normalization inside enterprise IDEs.

events.title: Cursor launches Builds — pre-warmed cloud agent environments, up to 3x faster agent startup, default-on Aug 17
events.summary: Cursor shipped Builds: hourly background-prepared environments so cloud agents boot up to 3x faster; broken builds never go active (fallback to last good); dashboard Builds tab with logs/SHAs. Becomes default for all environments on Aug 17 at no extra cost.
events.why_it_matters: Warm-environment startup removes the biggest latency tax on cloud coding agents; default-on for everyone Aug 17 makes it the baseline to benchmark against.

events.title: Contract-grade verifier for LLM-generated GPU kernels finds ~40% of accepted kernels broken
events.summary: Paper presents a verifier with twelve adversarial property-based gates (many tolerance-free) for AI-generated GPU kernels; 98.5% agreement with reference correctness code. Used to audit 2,638 publicly accepted machine-generated kernels: 39.5% broken beyond any tolerance argument, 62.1% had at least one violation; field-standard tests accepted 1,487 kernels the verifier rejected.
events.why_it_matters: Directly actionable warning for anyone shipping LLM-generated code validated only by loose tests — property-based adversarial gates should become part of kernel/code CI.

events.title: DARTree: speculative diffusion decoding with autoregressive draft trees — up to 9.73x lossless speedup
events.summary: Training-free extension of a pretrained autoregressive correction head from single chains to trees for diffusion speculative decoding; fixed-width candidate trees scored per-depth in one batch with best-first pruning. Up to 12.97 tokens accepted per verification round (+98.6% vs DFlash, +27.9% vs Domino) and up to 9.73x lossless speedup across 7 benchmarks.
events.why_it_matters: If reproducible, this is a material inference-serving acceleration technique; relevant to vLLM/SGLang-class stacks. No code repo yet.

events.title: DCD: decoupled contrastive decoding — 1.65-1.95x speedup with expert-aligned drafting, code released
events.summary: Decoupled Contrastive Decoding achieves 1.65-1.95x speedup over vanilla contrastive decoding using EAGLE3-style expert-aligned drafting, with code available on GitHub.
events.why_it_matters: Practical decoding-acceleration method with released code — lower verification cost than most decoding papers.
